subject: Clarify embed unit mapping to vectors and supported models
messages:

Subject: Embeddings price breakdown & model support (Synthora)

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Synthora is excited about the latency and density you showed. Procurement asked me to get a clear baseline rate card so we can map to our ingestion pipeline. A few specific asks: 

- Do you price embeddings per-vector or per-token for the hosted API? If per-vector, how do you map "embedding units" to vector dimensions (e.g., 1536 vs 4096)?
- Is there a different rate for text-generation tokens vs embedding tokens?
- Which embedding model families do you support today for hosted inference (model names and their typical output dimensions)?
- Any guidance on cost delta for moving from 1536-d to 4096-d vectors (ballpark multiplier)?

We have an initial batch of ~6M records/month and want to estimate monthly cost at baseline (no commitment) vs a 12-month committed discount. If you can send the ratecard and a short note on the mapping, I can route to finance.

Thanks,
Lena Ortiz

Synthora Analytics

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Embeddings price breakdown & model support (Synthora)

Hi Lena — great to hear from you and glad the demo landed well. Answering your questions below and attaching our baseline ratecard (PDF) for hosted embeddings.

Short answers up front:
- We charge for hosted embeddings on a per-vector basis. We also publish an equivalent "embedding unit" mapping to help customers with mixed-dimension workloads.
- Text-generation token pricing is separate (per-1k tokens); embedding vectors are priced per 1k vectors.
- Supported hosted embedding models (examples): redwood-embed-base-1536, redwood-embed-large-4096, open-embed-1024. See table in the attached ratecard.
- Cost delta: roughly linear with dimension. As a rule of thumb, cost per vector ≈ (dimension / 1536) * base_price_1536. So 4096-d is ~2.67x the 1536 baseline. We include tiered discounts for committed volumes.

Baseline hosted pricing (public, no commit) — excerpt:
- redwood-embed-base-1536: $0.80 per 1k vectors
- open-embed-1024: $0.60 per 1k vectors
- redwood-embed-large-4096: $2.15 per 1k vectors
- Text generation (for reference): $0.03 per 1k tokens (standard gen model)

Embedding unit mapping: a single "embedding unit" in our billing docs equals a 1536-d vector equivalent. For non-1536 dimensions we normalize: e.g. a 4096-d vector = 4096/1536 ≈ 2.666 units. The ratecard attached shows how we round for billing (nearest hundredth) and examples for common dims.

Commit discounts and packaging:
- 12-month commit: 15% off list for volumes >= 50M vectors/mo
- Volume slab pricing: 0-10M, 10-50M, >50M with increasing discounts and pricing per 1k vectors shown in the PDF.

I've attached: Redwood-Embed-Ratecard-v1.pdf (single-page summary) and a short quote template. If helpful I can also run a quick cost estimate for your 6M/month workload in a follow-up email.

Best,
Jordan Blake

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Subject: RE: Embeddings price breakdown & model support (Synthora)

Jordan / Neha — looping in some implementation notes for clarity (happy to jump on a short call with Synthora if needed).

- Vector-to-unit mapping: for customers with mixed dims we recommend choosing a billing anchor (1536 or 4096) and normalizing at ingest. We can also enable per-request model routing in the hosted API so you only pay the higher rate for requests that actually use the larger model.
- Latency/cost tradeoff: 4096-d vectors give better semantic density for some use-cases (fewer nearest-neighbor errors) but increase per-vector CPU/GPU work and therefore cost. In practice we see a 2.5–2.8x cost multiplier vs 1536 for typical workloads — depends on quantization and batching.
- Packaging suggestion for Synthora: start with a 3-slab commitment (0-10M / 10-50M / 50M+). Offer a starter 12-month pilot at 10% off for the first 10M, then standard 15% for >50M. This gives straight-line savings for them to validate model choice.

If you want, I can produce a simple cost sheet (CSV) that shows monthly spend under the three models (1536 vs 4096 vs mixed) using their 6M number.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
